bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for in-house upper/sole capacity to enable premiumization and IP protection; Maintaining strong ROCE (16.6%) and ROE (18%); Net debt expected to normalize by FY26 end; No dividend guidance disclosed
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk in Pant Nagar ramp-up; Delay in export market adoption; Oversupply in unorganized segment post-GST; High working capital intensity during peak season; Apparel pilot failure
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; focused on premiumization, capacity control, and long-term brand building; optimistic on GST tailwind and export potential; transparent on phasing and one-offs; no overpromising on margins or export targets
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 8% ASP growth was achieved despite a 12-15% revenue reduction from Flipkart/Myntra business model shift (freight now charged to consumer), indicating true underlying pricing power; Inventory build is seasonal and structural (MSME payment terms tightened to 45 days), not channel stuffing
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Return on Capital Employed of 22.8% is highlighted in the business snapshot; the annual ROCE series reads 18.5%, 30.6%, 23.2%, 19.2%, 22.3%, 22.4%, 22.8% against FY21 through TTM 3MFY27, defined as "EBIT divided by Capital Employed".
- Return on Equity series reads 9.0%, 29.3%, 23.9%, 14.9%, 17.2%, 18.1%, 18.0% against FY21 through TTM 3MFY27, defined as "TTM PAT by Average Shareholder's Equity".
- Net Debt / EBITDA series reads 1.1, 0.7, 0.6, 0.0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.0 against FY21 through TTM 3MFY27, with Net Debt defined as "Borrowings less Cash & Cash equivalent, excludes fixed deposits with banks".
- Reinvestment is framed qualitatively as "Investment in D2C & Tech initiatives" feeding the digitisation flywheel; the deck makes no mention of dividend, buyback or a stated payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Premium segment (INR 1,500+): 57.2% of mix (+12pp YoY); Women's: 16.2% of revenue (+2pp YoY); Kids: 4-5%; Accessories: 2-3%; Online: 5.7% growth (impacted by BBD timing shift); Distribution: 20% growth; Export: Nascent, under own brand, pilot in Sri Lanka/Morocco

business.body:
- Describes itself as the "#1 S&A Footwear Brand in India", with a footnote qualifying this as "Largest in terms of value and volume in FY21".
- Claims the "Widest Presence Across Price Segments" and "Largest Market Coverage Addressing 85%+ of the S&A Footwear Market", noting the Entry-to-Premium segments together comprise 85%+ of the S&A footwear market.
- States "Internal Strengths Curated Over the Years Across Product Design, Supply Chain, Distribution and Marketing is Onerous to Replicate", framed as five moat pillars: Superior Product Innovation and Design Capabilities, Vertically Integrated Manufacturing Ecosystem, Omni-Channel Customer Experience, Innovative Marketing Capabilities and Digitization of Sales Process.
- Reach cited as 31,000+ retailers/retail touchpoints across 850+ districts and 28 states, 260+ distributors, 2,350+ LFS counters, 305+ EBOs and a 200+ employee internal sales force; described as "Leading Footwear Brand on Flipkart, Myntra and Nykaa".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Corporate history] A footnote records that the INR 1,000 mm revenue milestone was "crossed by Nikhil International, whose business was subsequently acquired pursuant to a business succession agreement dated Mar 22, 2017".
- [NCLT merger] Footnote states: "Pursuant to NCLT merger order, EBITDA and PAT for FY'21, FY22, Q1 FY'23 has been revised to give effect to the order."
- [Brand event] "Shoe case 2026" is presented as a brand transformation event unveiling Campus' refreshed brand identity, launching ELAN neo-casual footwear and convening distributor partners nationwide.
- [Elan campaign] The Elan launch is claimed to have drawn "11.7 million+ views: Across Instagram and digital platforms within the first month" and "18 high-quality content pieces driving 127K+ interactions", rolled out across digital, social, retail, Amazon and Myntra with the Amazon Made in India series.
- [Industry source] All market-size and market-share data is attributed to Technopak Advisors' "Report on Footwear Retail in India" dated April 07, 2022, which the deck itself says has not been independently verified.

deepdive.thesis: Campus delivered 16% revenue growth and 40% PAT growth in Q2FY26 driven by premium segment expansion (ASP up 8%) and distribution channel strength, with normalized EBITDA margin at 16% despite phasing in marketing spend; the key inflection is in-house upper capacity expansion enabling IP control and premium pricing, positioning the company to capture share from unorganized players post-GST rationalization.

drhp.business: Campus Activewear designs, manufactures, markets, sells and distributes sports and athleisure footwear, apparel and accessories (socks, backpacks, caps, belts) for men, women and children, sold under the Campus brand and its new sub-brand ELAN by Campus. It serves a broad Indian consumer base across Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities through e-commerce platforms, authorised distributors, exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) and multi-brand outlets (MBOs), with a small export presence.
drhp.end_markets: Pan-India, Tier 1/2/3 cities|International (6 countries, exports ~0.30% of turnover)
drhp.expansion: Commercial production of premium uppers commenced at the Pantnagar facility in January 2026, adding to the Company's integrated premium capacity, while the Paonta Sahib upper facility stabilised fully during FY26. In January 2026 the Company also launched a new athleisure apparel range, initially across 60+ Exclusive Brand Outlets, the brand website and on Amazon/Myntra, as a natural extension of its design capability, brand equity and distribution network. Management states that land and infrastructure are already in place to add manufacturing capacity quickly as demand grows.

risks.note: Stiff competition from well-resourced global athletic footwear brands operating in India and emerging domestic D2C players; aggressive pricing, promotional intensity and rapid product iteration by competitors can compress margins and raise customer acquisition costs.

Operational efficiency depends on consistent availability of high-quality inputs (EVA, PU, synthetic uppers, adhesives); disruption or quality deterioration in the supply chain could cause production delays, higher costs and lower consumer satisfaction.

Input costs are sensitive to global commodity movements, particularly petrochemical derivatives underpinning synthetic materials; sharp cost increases may compress margins if not passed through to consumers in a timely manner.

Maintaining product relevance in a market shaped by rapidly shifting consumer style preferences requires sustained design innovation and responsive supply chain execution; misreading trend direction could hurt sales velocity and inventory utilisation.

Changes in import duties, BIS compliance standards, GST structures and other regulatory frameworks can alter the Company's cost base and necessitate pricing adjustments; the unresolved inverted-duty structure on certain raw materials remains a cost overhang, against which refund claims have begun to be filed.

Inflation spikes, interest rate increases, currency depreciation or geopolitical disruptions can weaken consumer sentiment and reduce discretionary spending, directly impacting demand for branded and aspirational products.
Proliferation of counterfeit and imitation products, particularly in mass-market and online channels, poses a risk to brand integrity, consumer trust and revenue.
As the Company expands its digital and D2C operations, managing cybersecurity risk and consumer data privacy remains a critical area requiring sustained investment and vigilance.
